description_full: Antero Resources Corporation, an independent oil and natural gas company, engages in the development, production, exploration, and acquisition of natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), and oil properties in the United States. It operates in three segments: Exploration and Production; Marketing; and Equity Method Investment in Antero Midstream. As of December 31, 2025, the company had approximately 537,000 net acres in the Appalachian Basin; and approximately 168,000 net acres in the Upper Devonian Shale. Its gathering and compression systems also comprise 731 miles of gas gathering pipelines in the Appalachian Basin. The company was formerly known as Antero Resources Appalachian Corporation and changed its name to Antero Resources Corporation in June 2013. Antero Resources Corporation was incorporated in 2002 and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.

financial_summary: Antero Resources Corporation is a large-cap energy business with a $11.1B market cap on $5.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -10% over the past three years and +3% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $1.6B in free cash flow — roughly 31 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.57× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 10.0×.

Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 4.4% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
